name: Turso
description: In-process SQL database compatible with SQLite, written in Rust.
summary: Turso explicitly welcomes developing with AI coding agents, provided contributors understand the code they submit, self-review it, and can explain and defend their pull requests. AI-generated tests must be verified to fail without the change, AI-written PR summaries must be rewritten in the contributor's own words, and people unfamiliar with an area are encouraged to file a bug report rather than send an AI-generated fix.

evidence.quote: You're welcome to develop Turso with AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode. Used well, they can help you explore the codebase, draft tests, and polish your contributions.

We expect you to understand the code you submit. The best AI-assisted contributions come from people who treat the agent as a collaborator, not a substitute: you direct the work, review it critically, and own the result.
A PR you can explain and defend is far more valuable than a large one you can't.
Always self-review your code before submitting - make sure it's correct and follows the existing code standards in this repo.
**Include regression tests.** Verify that your tests actually FAIL without your changes — this is especially important when the tests are AI-generated.
**Keep it small and focused.** Describe the change in your own words, or heavily edit any AI-generated summary so it reads naturally and accurately.

**Contribute in areas you understand.** If you spot a bug in something like the MVCC or b-tree layer but aren't familiar with it, the most helpful thing you can do is file a clear bug report rather than submit an AI-generated fix.
**Keep it small and focused.** Describe the change in your own words, or heavily edit any AI-generated summary so it reads naturally and accurately.
